theme.title: Swat team
theme.subtitle: Blocked-shot records
theme.recap: Blocks were first counted in 1973–74, and the records include Elmore Smith's 11 in a half and Dwight Howard's nine in a Finals game.

questions.prompt: Dwight Howard set the Finals record for blocks in a game in 2009. How many?

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: giving him a single-game NBA Finals record with 9 blocked shots

funFacts.text: Orlando's center threatened Los Angeles near the end, but Derek Fisher hit a crucial late three.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Trevor Ariza was able to hit a 3-pointer as the shot clock expired

funFacts.text: The Magic squandered foul-shot opportunities in a tight Game 4 despite leading at halftime.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: but were unable to increase the lead due to poor free-throw shooting

funFacts.text: Orlando had earned its very first NBA Finals game victory only in the preceding game.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: This win marked the first Finals win in Magic franchise history

questions.prompt: In the first season blocks were counted, Elmore Smith set the record for blocks in a half. How many?

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: 11 blocks in a half, setting the NBA record. 6 blocks in one quarter; 5 blocks in the other quarter

funFacts.text: Smith's record came in a Los Angeles Lakers victory over Portland during the league's first season tracking blocks.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Elmore Smith  | Los Angeles Lakers  | October 28, 1973  | Portland Trail Blazers

funFacts.text: That same performance also included a hefty rebounding total and a triple-double.
Only a few days earlier, Smith had also posted a huge blocked-shot game against Detroit.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Elmore Smith  (2)  | Los Angeles Lakers  | October 26, 1973

questions.prompt: Manute Bol set the record for blocks in a quarter in December 1985. How many?

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: 8 blocks in the first quarter, setting the NBA record, and 11 blocks in the first half, tying the NBA record

funFacts.text: Bol set his mark while playing for Washington in an overtime victory against the Milwaukee Bucks.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Washington Bullets  | December 12, 1985  | Milwaukee Bucks

funFacts.text: The rookie also reached a huge first-half swat total in the same game against Milwaukee.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: 11 blocks in the first half, tying the NBA record

funFacts.text: Bol later repeated the feat in a fourth quarter against Indiana during his Washington years.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: 8 blocks in the fourth quarter, tying the NBA record

questions.prompt: In March 2001, Toronto set what was then the NBA record for team blocks in a game. How many?
questions.note: 23, an NBA record at the time.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: The Raptors combined for 23 blocks, an NBA record at the time

funFacts.text: Toronto reserve Keon Clark supplied the biggest share of the swats despite not starting against Atlanta.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Keon Clark  | Toronto Raptors  | March 23, 2001

funFacts.text: Clark astonishingly committed no personal fouls while sending shot after shot away.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Did not commit a personal foul; holds the NBA record for most blocks

funFacts.text: The Raptors' defensive masterpiece came against the Atlanta Hawks in a comfortable win.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Atlanta Hawks  | 112–86

questions.prompt: David Robinson's 1994 quadruple-double included 10 blocks. How many points did he score?

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: with 34 points, 10 rebounds, 10 assists, and 10 blocks against the Detroit Pistons on February 17, 1994

funFacts.text: Robinson joined an exceptionally small group of players who recorded double figures in four statistical categories.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: one of only four players to have officially recorded a quadruple-double

funFacts.text: The Admiral had attended the Naval Academy and was so tall that he could not serve aboard Navy ships.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: which later prevented him from serving on any U.S. Navy ships

funFacts.text: Robinson won championships both before and after the turn of the millennium, playing his entire career in San Antonio.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: 2× NBA champion (1999, 2003)
